title: Find the real subject
intro: Sam is proofreading the school newspaper before it goes to print. Every story has one grammar slip.
hook: Cross out the phrases in the middle to find what has to agree. Then check pronouns, tense, and modifiers.

steps.prompt: Story 1, the garden club: 'The flowers in the community garden ______ every spring.'
steps.why: Cross out 'in the community garden.' The flowers bloom: plural subject, plural verb.

steps.prompt: Story 2, the team: 'Each of the players ___ a new jersey.' Type the verb: has or have.
lines: Each of the players ___ a new jersey.
steps.why: Each is singular. Of the players is just a phrase in between.

steps.prompt: Story 3, the science fair: sort these by whether the possessive is right.

cards.text: the museum and its new galleries

steps.why: Its means belonging to it; it's means it is. Plural owners take s-apostrophe, and pronouns must match their nouns.

steps.prompt: Story 4, the hike. Tap the sentence Sam should fix.
lines: Walking through the forest at dawn, the hikers heard birdsong.
Hoping to see the comet, my brother stayed up late.
Originally designed to carry mail, passengers later rode the airplane.
Having trained for months, Ana finished in record time.
steps.why: The opening phrase describes the airplane, so 'the airplane' must come right after the comma, not 'passengers.'

steps.prompt: Story 5, Sam's checklist. Put the checks in the order Sam uses them.
items: Find the subject and cross out phrases in between
Make the verb agree with the subject
Check tense against time words like yesterday or since
Check that pronouns match the nouns they replace
steps.why: Subject first, because agreement depends on it; then tense; then pronouns.

steps.prompt: Last story: 'By the time the guests arrived, the hosts ______ all the food.'
steps.why: One past event finished before another: past perfect.

keys: Cross out phrases between the subject and verb.
Its (belonging to it) vs. it's (it is); plural owners: s-apostrophe.
An opening phrase must be followed by the thing it describes.

recall.prompt: 'Neither the coach nor the players ___ ready.'
recall.why: Agree with the closer subject: players.

recall.prompt: What's the first step on a subject-verb agreement question?
recall.answer: Find the real subject by crossing out the phrases in between.
